chunks: And in the narration of al-Mufaḍḍal ibn ʿUmar from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:

Regarding a man who had relations with his wife while he was fasting and she was fasting, he said: “If he forced her, then two expiations are upon him. If she consented to him, then one expiation is upon him and one expiation is upon her. If he compelled her, then upon him is fifty lashes, half of the prescribed punishment. And if she consented to him, he is given twenty-five lashes and she is given twenty-five lashes.”

key_terms.اسْتَكْرَهَهَا: he forced her against her will
key_terms.كَفَّارَةٌ: one expiation required for violating the fast
key_terms.نِصْفِ الْحَدِّ: half of the fixed legal punishment

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a fasting husband has intercourse with his fasting wife during Ramadan, whether by coercion or mutual consent?
ai.summary: This hadith gives legal rulings for intercourse during the fast of Ramadan when both spouses are fasting. It distinguishes between coercion and mutual consent, assigning expiation and corporal punishment according to each case, showing the legal seriousness of intentionally violating the fast and the difference between compulsion and willingness.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1889 - In the narration of al-Mufaddal ibn Umar from Abu Abdullah (as)

regarding a man who had relations with his wife while both were fasting, Imam (as) said:
"If he forced her, he must bear two expiations. If she consented, then he must bear one expiation and she must bear one expiation. If he forced her, he is to be lashed fifty times, half the prescribed punishment. If she consented, he is to be lashed twenty-five times, and she is to be lashed twenty-five times as well."
